chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) in the year two hundred and twenty-five, bidding farewell to the House after the sun had risen, and performing Tawaf of the House, touching the Yamani Corner during each circuit. So when it was the seventh circuit, he touched it and touched the Stone, and wiped with his hand, then wiped his face with his hand.

Then he went to the Maqam (Standing Place of Ibrahim), so he performed two cycles of Salat behind it. Then he went out to the back of the Ka'bah, to the Multazam, so he adhered to the House, and uncovered the cloth from his belly, then paused upon it for a long time, supplicating. Then he went out from the door of al-Hannatayn and faced it.

He said, So I also saw him in the year two hundred and seventeen bidding farewell to the House at night, touching the Yamani Corner and the Black Stone during each circuit. So when he was in the seventh circuit, he adhered to the House at the back of the Ka'bah, near to the Yamani Corner, and above the elongated Stone, and uncovered the cloth from his belly. Then he went to the Stone, so he kissed it, and wiped it, and went to the Maqam, so he performed Salat behind it. Then he went and did not return to the House.
And his pausing at the Multazam was of a measurement of what some of our companions take to perform Tawaf of seven circuits, and some of them eight.

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِي: The Yamani Corner of the Ka'bah, touched during Tawaf
key_terms.الْمَقَام: The Standing Place of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَم: The section of the Ka'bah wall between the door and the Yamani Corner, where pilgrims adhere to supplicate

ai.seo_question: What are the specific ritual steps for bidding farewell to the Ka'bah according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the ritual significance of 'Tadi' (bidding farewell) to the Ka'bah, a practice emphasized in Shia jurisprudence to conclude the pilgrimage with heightened devotion. It details Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) specific actions, such as touching the Yamani Corner and Black Stone during every circuit and the final supplication at the Multazam, illustrating the integration of physical acts with spiritual reflection. This narration serves as a primary source for the recommended etiquette of concluding Hajj or Umrah, reinforcing the connection between the pilgrim and the Divine House.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Mahziyar who said,

‘I saw Abu Ja’farasws the 2nd in the year two hundred and twenty five, bidding farewell to the House (Kabah) after the rising of the sun, and performing Tawaaf of the House Kabah, touching Al-Yamani corner during each circuit. So when it was the seventh circuit, heasws touched it and touched the (Black) Stone, and wiped it with hisasws hand, then wiped hisasws face with hisasws hand.

Then heasws went to the Standing Place (of Ibrahimas), so he performed Salaat behind it, by two Cycles. Then heasws went out to the back of the Kabah, to Al-Multazam, so heasws adhered to the House, and uncovered the cloth from hisasws belly, then paused upon it for a long time, supplicating. Then heasws went out from the door of Al-Hannatayn and faced it.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I (also) saw himasws in the year two hundred and seventeen bidding farewell to the House (Kabah) at night, touching Al-Yamani corner, and the Black Stone during each circuit. So when heasws was in the seventh circuit, heasws adhered to the House at the back of the Kabah, near to the Yamani corner, and above the (Black) Stone by the rectangular stone, and uncovered the cloth from his belly. Then he went to the (Black) Stone), so heasws kissed it, and wiped it, and went to the Standing Place (of Ibrahimas), and heasws performed Salaat behind it. Then heasws went and did not return to the House (Kabah),
and it was hisasws pausing at Al-Multazam of a measurement of what some of our companions take to perform Tawaaf of seven circuits, and some of them eight’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from Ali ibn Mahziyar who has said the following:

“I saw Abu Ja`far, the second ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the year 225 Hijriy, say farewell to the House after sunrise. He performed Tawaf around the House, touched al-Yemaniy corner every time he walked around the House. During the seventh, the last shawt (walking around the House) he touched that corner and the Black Stone. He touched with his hand and then wiped his hand over his face.

He then went behind al-Maqam (station of Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam ) then performed two Rak £ at salat (prayer). He then went behind al-Ka £ bah to al-Multazam. He kept his belly, without any covering, attached to the wall of the House. He then stood up for a long time, praying. He then went out through the door of al-Hannatin and turned his face to the House.

I had seen him in the year 217 Hijriy saying farewell to the House during the night. He touched al-Yemaniy corner and the Black Stone every time he walked around the House. During the seventh shawt, he kept himself very close to the House at its backside near al-Yemaniy corner over the rectangular stone. He kept his belly attached to the wall of al-Ka‘bah without any covering. He then went to the Black Stone, kissed it, touched it and then went behind al-Maqam of Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam and performed two Rak £ at salat (prayer). He then left and did not return to the House.
His standing near al-Multazam was for such a long time as some of our people’s walking seven times and others’ eight times around the Ka £ bah.’”
